QoS is derived from the resource spec, not set directly. Check the current verdict with `kubectl -n dojo-qos get pods -l app=cache -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.qosClass}'` — you'll see Burstable because the pods have requests but no limits.

Guaranteed needs `requests == limits` for BOTH cpu AND memory, on EVERY container in the pod. The setup gave you `cpu: 100m` / `memory: 64Mi` requests — add a `limits` block with the exact same two values.

Patch and roll out: `kubectl -n dojo-qos patch deploy cache --type merge -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"cache","resources":{"requests":{"cpu":"100m","memory":"64Mi"},"limits":{"cpu":"100m","memory":"64Mi"}}}]}}}}'`. Wait for the new pods, then re-check `status.qosClass` — it must read Guaranteed.
